Fixes a batch of GitHub issues in parallel worktrees through a background Workflow, one PR each, optionally merged on green CI.

What it does

issues-workflow hands a batch of open GitHub issues to a background Workflow. Each issue gets its own agent in its own git worktree, which reproduces the bug with a test, fixes it, runs the checks and review skills, and opens one PR. Your main session only scouts and launches, so its context stays small.

When to use it

  • You want several issues fixed in parallel: "work these issues in workflow mode".
  • You want the fixes done without spending main-session tokens.
  • You want the PRs merged one at a time on green CI, each rebased on the one before.

How it works

  • Lists the repo's open issues and picks the ones you name. With no list, it takes the bugs and tells you which it left out.
  • Asks once whether to merge on green CI or leave the PRs open.
  • Launches workflow.js with args such as repo, issues, merge, base, reviewSkills, prSkill, serial and checks. The skill file lists them all.
  • An agent that finds the issue is not a bug, or needs a product decision, stops and reports back instead of guessing.
  • Merges run serially: rebase, watch CI with gh run watch, fix up to three times, then squash-merge.

Requirements

  • Claude Code with the Workflow tool.
  • git and the GitHub CLI (gh), authenticated.
  • Optional: the code-review plugin from claude-plugins-official (/plugin install code-review@claude-plugins-official). It is the default review step; agents skip review skills that are not installed.
  • Optional: any PR skill passed as prSkill, such as the pr plugin from this repo.

Work a batch of open GitHub issues in parallel through a background Workflow, one agent per issue in its own git worktree, one PR each, optionally merged one at a time on green CI. Use when the user asks to work open issues "in workflow mode", "in parallel", or without spending main-session tokens.

---
name: issues-workflow
description: Work a batch of open GitHub issues in parallel through a background Workflow, one agent per issue in its own git worktree, one PR each, optionally merged one at a time on green CI. Use when the user asks to work open issues "in workflow mode", "in parallel", or without spending main-session tokens.
---

The main session only scouts and launches. The agents do the fixing, so the main context stays small.

1. Find the repo with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,defaultBranchRef`, then list the issues with `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,labels,assignees`.
2. Pick the issues the user asked for. With no explicit list, take the bugs and name the ones left out (enhancements, deferred).
3. Ask once, unless the user's memory or CLAUDE.md already answers it: should PRs be merged on green CI, or left open for review?
4. Launch `Workflow({scriptPath: "<this skill's directory>/workflow.js", args})`, with the absolute path.
5. Do not poll. When the completion notification arrives, report per issue: PR, merged or not, blockers. A `blocked` or `not_a_bug` result is a question for the user.

## args

- `repo` (required): `owner/name`. Pass it explicitly, since a local `origin` can point at a renamed repo.
- `issues` (required): issue numbers.
- `merge`: `true` to rebase, wait for CI and squash-merge each PR in turn. Default `false`, PRs stay open.
- `base`: target branch, default `main`.
- `context`: files or instructions every fix agent reads first (handoff notes, a CONTRIBUTING file, check quirks).
- `reviewSkills`: skills run in order before the PR, default `["code-review --fix"]`. Agents skip any that are not installed.
- `prSkill`: a skill that opens the PR in the team's format. Default plain `gh pr create`.
- `mergeSuffix`: text appended to the merge command, for a hook that asks for a confirmation marker.
- `model`: model for the agents. Default: the session's model.
- `serial`: `true` runs one fix agent at a time. Use it when parallel test runs overload the machine.
- `checks`: how to run the checks on this machine (worker caps, scoped specs). Overrides the agents' defaults.
- `wip`: `{issue: "/abs/path.patch"}`, an interrupted run's diff the agent applies as a draft.

Example:

```json
{"repo": "acme/api", "issues": [408, 409], "merge": true,
 "context": ["CONTRIBUTING.md"], "reviewSkills": ["code-review --fix", "simplify"]}
```

## Notes

- Each agent runs in a git worktree. Worktree guard hooks often refuse compound git commands (pipes, `&&`, wrappers), so the prompts tell agents to keep git commands simple.
- Merges run one at a time, so each PR rebases on the one merged before it. Translation files are the usual conflict.
- Resume after a crash: `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` with the same args.

export const meta = {
  name: 'issues-workflow',
  description: 'Fix GitHub issues in parallel worktrees, one PR each, optionally merged one at a time on green CI',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per issue in its own worktree: test, fix, checks, review, PR' },
    { title: 'Merge', detail: 'serialized: rebase on main, green CI, squash-merge (only when args.merge)' },
  ],
}

const A = args || {}
if (!A.repo || !Array.isArray(A.issues) || !A.issues.length) {
  throw new Error('args needs {repo: "owner/name", issues: [numbers]}')
}
const REPO = A.repo
const BASE = A.base || 'main'
const CONTEXT = A.context || []
const REVIEW = A.reviewSkills || ['code-review --fix']
const PR_SKILL = A.prSkill || null
const MERGE_SUFFIX = A.mergeSuffix ? ` ${A.mergeSuffix}` : ''
const MODEL = A.model || undefined
const WIP = A.wip || {}
const CHECKS = A.checks || null

const GIT_RULE = `A worktree guard hook may refuse git commands it cannot verify. Run git one simple command per call, from the worktree root: no pipes, no &&, no wrappers around git.`

const PR_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    issue: { type: 'number' },
    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pr_opened', 'blocked', 'not_a_bug'] },
    pr: { type: 'number' },
    branch: { type: 'string' },
    note: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['issue', 'status', 'note'],
}

const MERGE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    pr: { type: 'number' },
    merged: { type: 'boolean' },
    note: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['pr', 'merged', 'note'],
}

const contextStep = CONTEXT.length
  ? `\n- these project notes, which take precedence over your defaults:\n${CONTEXT.map((c) => `  - ${c}`).join('\n')}`
  : ''

const fixPrompt = (n) => `You own GitHub issue #${n} on ${REPO}. You run in your own git worktree; other agents fix other issues in parallel in theirs.

${GIT_RULE}

Read first:
- \`gh issue view ${n} --repo ${REPO} --comments\`. Any "possible cause" in it is a hypothesis: read the code path end to end.${contextStep}

Then:
1. \`git fetch origin ${BASE}\`, then branch from origin/${BASE}: \`fix/${n}-<short-slug>\`.${WIP[n] ? `
   An earlier interrupted run left work in progress for this issue: \`git apply ${WIP[n]}\`. Treat it as a draft: read it against the issue and the code, keep what holds, fix or drop the rest.` : ''}
2. Reproduce with a failing test, then fix the root cause. If it is not a bug, or the fix needs a product decision, stop and return not_a_bug or blocked with the reason. Do not comment on the issue.
3. Run the project's own checks (lint, typecheck, tests, build) for every part you touched. All must pass.${CHECKS ? ` How to run them on this machine (it overrides your defaults): ${CHECKS}` : ''}
4. Review, in this order, with the Skill tool: ${REVIEW.join(', then ')}. Skip any skill that is not installed. Re-run the checks after any change.
5. Commit following the style of \`git log\`, push, and open the PR ${PR_SKILL ? `with the Skill ${PR_SKILL}` : 'with `gh pr create`'} using \`--repo ${REPO} --head <branch> --base ${BASE}\`. The body says "Closes #${n}". Do not merge.

Return the PR number and branch.`

const mergePrompt = (r) => `Merge PR #${r.pr} (branch ${r.branch}, closes #${r.issue}) on ${REPO}. PRs from the same batch may have merged into ${BASE} just before you.

${GIT_RULE}

1. \`git fetch origin\`, check out ${r.branch}, rebase on origin/${BASE}. Resolve conflicts keeping both sides' intent (for translation or config files, keep both sides' keys). Re-run the checks for the touched parts, then \`git push --force-with-lease\`.
2. Watch CI: \`gh run list --repo ${REPO} --branch ${r.branch}\`, then \`gh run watch <id> --repo ${REPO} --exit-status\`. No sleep loops.
3. If CI fails, read the logs, fix, push, watch again. Stop after 3 honest attempts.
4. On green: \`gh pr merge ${r.pr} --repo ${REPO} --squash --delete-branch${MERGE_SUFFIX}\`.

Return whether it merged.`

let mergeChain = Promise.resolve()

const fix = (n) => agent(fixPrompt(n), { label: `fix #${n}`, phase: 'Fix', isolation: 'worktree', schema: PR_SCHEMA, model: MODEL })

// serial: one fix agent at a time, for machines that cannot take parallel test runs
let fixChain = Promise.resolve()
const fixStage = A.serial
  ? (n) => {
      const run = fixChain.then(() => fix(n))
      fixChain = run.catch(() => null)
      return run
    }
  : fix

const results = await pipeline(
  A.issues,
  fixStage,
  (r) => {
    if (!A.merge || !r || r.status !== 'pr_opened' || !r.pr) return r
    const run = mergeChain.then(() =>
      agent(mergePrompt(r), { label: `merge #${r.pr}`, phase: 'Merge', isolation: 'worktree', schema: MERGE_SCHEMA, model: MODEL }))
    mergeChain = run.catch(() => null)
    return run.then((m) => ({ ...r, merge: m }))
  },
)

return results.map((r, i) => r || { issue: A.issues[i], status: 'agent_failed', note: 'agent returned nothing' })
